findings.statement: The role × per-role-knob axis is encoded in three orientations with no single mechanism. (a) Knob-major: six submodels (ModelsConfig, BudgetsConfig, TurnsConfig, EffortConfig, TimeoutsConfig, BackendsConfig) each restate the 11 role names, 66 role-keyed fields in all. TimeoutsConfig also mixes two non-role knobs (startup_grace_secs, working_idle_secs) into the role namespace. (b) Role-major: UnblockAutoConfig carries model/budget_usd/timeout_seconds/max_turns/effort/backend for one role. (c) Flat: watcher_model/watcher_rotation_budget_usd/watcher_max_turns/watcher_effort/watcher_backend, plus the deprecated simple_task_budget_usd/simple_task_max_turns scalars migrated by a validator. Role names have three vocabularies: agents/roles.py ROLES (9 full names), ModelsConfig (11 collapsed names) and shared KNOWN_ROLE_NAMES (12, the union). The reviewer* collapse is implemented twice: routing.py::_config_key and an inline startswith('reviewer') in workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._invoke for timeouts and backends. Per-role reads use getattr/hasattr with defaults, so a missing field falls back silently. _validate_models_in_allowlist covers models.* and unblock_auto.model but not watcher_model.
findings.proposal: One role-keyed table: RoleSettings(model, effort, budget_usd, max_turns, timeout_secs, backend) and roles: dict[RoleName, RoleSettings], with RoleName a closed enum shared with ROLES and KNOWN_ROLE_NAMES. The reviewer* collapse becomes one declared mapping. unblock_auto and the watcher become entries. Allowlist and completeness-against-ROLES validation run once over the table.
findings.next_change: Adding a dispatch role (a new reviewer variant, a planner) or a new per-role knob (e.g. per-role retries). The agent must add a field to each of six submodels and add the name to KNOWN_ROLE_NAMES in shared/. It must decide in two places whether the reviewer* collapse applies, and it must know the watcher and unblock-auto roles hold the same knobs in two other shapes. A missed submodel field is not an error: resolve_route's hasattr skip uses the role default, workflow's getattr falls back to invocation_timeout or 'claude', and the role runs on defaults. A model set through the watcher's flat field bypasses the allowlist the other roles get. The only drift guard is ModelsConfig fields ⊆ KNOWN_ROLE_NAMES.

findings.statement: The scheduler files escalations through three unrelated mechanisms. (1) Seven SchedulerCallbacks hooks are awaited at 11 call sites; the Harness builds the Escalation: on_external_dep_block, on_delivered_check_block, on_starvation_warn/resolve and on_warm_base_warn/promote_l2/resolve. (2) Two sites build Escalation objects inline and submit to self.escalation_queue: _file_fm_read_storm_escalation and _maybe_escalate_backfill_overstay_rate. That attribute is injected by harness.py after construction. Each site has its own sentinel task id (a class attribute in one, a module constant in the other), its own has_open_l1 dedup and a function-local 'from escalation.models import Escalation'. (3) trigger_retry_cap_exhausted takes the queue as a parameter even though self.escalation_queue exists. Severity, level, category and dedup conventions therefore live partly in harness.py's _block_and_escalate_* and _file_* methods and partly inline in scheduler.py.
findings.proposal: Give the Scheduler one constructor-injected escalation port, e.g. file(kind, subject, summary, detail, level, dedup_key) and resolve(dedup_key), implemented once in the harness. Route the three inline sites and the seven callbacks through it so the level, dedup and category policy has one home.
findings.next_change: Adding a scheduler watchdog that pages someone; the scheduler already has seven. The agent must choose, with no stated rule, between three paths. One is an eighth SchedulerCallbacks field plus a Harness method wired in Harness.__init__. Another is an inline Escalation against self.escalation_queue, which is None until the harness injects it and is skipped with a warning in bare-Scheduler tests. The third is a queue parameter. It must read harness.py to learn which level/severity/dedup each existing path uses. A wrong choice (an inline level=1 where the sibling path is born-at-L2, or a missing has_open_l1) is caught by no test that asserts the mechanism, because unit tests run with callbacks None and escalation_queue None, and every path treats that as a logged no-op.

findings.statement: The scheduler state snapshot is a cross-process contract held together by string keys. Scheduler.get_state_snapshot builds a 13-key untyped dict, and _write_snapshot_best_effort writes it to <project_root>/data/orchestrator/scheduler_state.json. fused-memory rebuilds that path independently (mcp_tools/scheduler_state.py::read_scheduler_state) and hand-maintains an empty skeleton of 10 keys. The skeleton lacks pin_reservations (task 6040), requeue_cooldowns (task 3317) and lock_depth. The dashboard (dashboard/data/scheduler.py) and fused-memory services/live_workflow_detector.py read keys by .get('<key>') string literals. shared/ holds no type or constant for the snapshot.
findings.proposal: A typed SchedulerStateSnapshot (pydantic model or TypedDict) and the relative-path constant in shared/. The producer serialises through it, fused-memory and the dashboard parse through it, and the skeleton becomes SchedulerStateSnapshot.empty().
findings.next_change: Adding or renaming a snapshot key, as tasks 3317 and 6040 each did; exposing backfill grants or the pin-blocked state would be next. The agent must find readers in two other packages by grep. The absent-file skeleton silently omits new keys, so a reader written against the producer's shape gets a KeyError or a wrong default only on a cold start with no file, a path the orchestrator's own tests never exercise. A producer-side rename breaks nothing in its own package.

findings.statement: The remote merge-verify lane-lock protocol is implemented inline in a click command, alongside a second copy in git_ops. cli.py::verify_merge is 280 lines, 125 of them comments. It acquires and releases the shared lane flock and a transitional compat co-lock, writes, removes and reads the shared holder-pgid rendezvous, and releases the lane lock before acquire_host_verify_worktree because reset_persistent_merge_worktree re-takes the same inode. It then re-takes the lane lock for the build only. GitOps.merge_verify_lease (217 lines, 75 comment lines) implements the same lane-lock + holder-pgid protocol for the local lane. Both describe the compat co-lock as dropped by 'a post-rollout follow-up'. cli.py::cancel_verify (95 lines, 45 comment lines) owns the identity-gated cleanup of the same fixed holder key.
findings.proposal: One lane-lease async context manager in verify_cancel (or git_ops), parameterised by holder recording and the compat co-lock, used by both the local lease and the remote CLI. The click command shrinks to argument parsing plus 'async with lease: run_merge_verify_on_worktree'. The lock-lifetime rationale moves to that function's docstring, where a single copy is kept.
findings.next_change: The documented follow-up is to drop the .merge_verify.lock compat co-lock or change the holder-pgid rendezvous. It must be applied identically to GitOps.merge_verify_lease (local lane), cli.verify_merge (remote lane) and cancel_verify's cleanup rule. The agent must also preserve the split lane-lock lifetime, a cross-file constraint stated only in comments: verify_merge must not hold the lane lock across acquire_host_verify_worktree. A version that edits one copy deadlocks or loses mutual exclusion only on the remote laptop host, which the local test suite does not exercise.

findings.statement: Route resolution and recording exist in two copies: one for TaskWorkflow._invoke and one for the five out-of-band dispatch sites. routing_dispatch.py mirrors workflow.py helper by helper: _trailing_24h_window ≙ workflow._trailing_24h_window, _ceiling_spend_by_model ≙ TaskWorkflow._ceiling_spend_by_model, _out_of_band_inputs_digest ≙ workflow._routing_inputs_digest, and resolve_and_record_route's mirror/event/update_task block ≙ TaskWorkflow._record_routing_decision. Each docstring says 'Mirrors workflow.py::…'. The stated cause is that workflow.py was outside the task's lock scope; the module docstring says 'a documented follow-up can dedupe it'. The copies have already diverged: the out-of-band RouteInputs never sets scope_capacity, while _invoke passes _scope_capacity_snapshot().
findings.proposal: Make TaskWorkflow._invoke call routing_dispatch.resolve_and_record_route, passing its scope_capacity snapshot and plan shape, and delete the four workflow.py copies.
findings.next_change: Changing what a routing decision records (a field on RoutingDecisionMirror or on the routing_decision event payload, or the 24h ceiling window) must be made in workflow.py and routing_dispatch.py together. An agent working in either file sees no import of the other, and no test asserts parity between in-band and out-of-band emissions, so the event schema can drift per dispatch path.

findings.statement: Two config knobs each govern a second, undocumented behaviour because the change that needed a new knob was locked out of config.py. delivered_checks.max_checks_per_tick (documented as 'uncached delivered-checks evaluated per tick') also caps the concurrent get_task fetch fan-out in _phase_backfill_terminal_dep_records. The code says 'a dedicated cap would need a new config.py field, outside this task's scheduler.py-only scope'. max_external_dep_unresolved_cycles (documented as the external-dep sentinel escalation threshold) also sets the local-backfill degradation warning threshold in _phase_backfill_dep_status, where the code says 'A dedicated max_local_backfill_unresolved_cycles field is deferred (config.py is out of scope)'.
findings.proposal: Give each behaviour its own field, delivered_checks.max_record_fetches_per_tick and max_local_backfill_unresolved_cycles, defaulting to today's shared values and placed in RELOADABLE_FIELDS beside their siblings.
findings.next_change: An operator or agent raises max_checks_per_tick so a dep with many checks can resolve, and thereby also widens the per-tick asyncio.gather of get_task fetches against fused-memory. Or they lower max_external_dep_unresolved_cycles to escalate cross-project deps sooner, and local-backfill degradation warnings start firing sooner too. Neither knob's documentation reveals the second effect; only a grep of scheduler.py does. Nothing catches the unintended retune.

findings.statement: plan-tools' markup-sink wiring is shaped around monkeypatching rather than injection. create_server builds its escalation sink and fact journal from module-level functions (_markup_project_root, _escalation_channel, _markup_fact_journal, _markup_plan_stamp, _markup_escalation_sink, _markup_subject_task_id). These are reached through lambdas that look the global name up at call time, and the docstrings explain that the indirection exists 'so a test that substitutes either seam steers an already-built sink'. verdict_tools.py repeats the pattern. Four test files patch 11 distinct private plan_tools names plus plan_tools.subprocess.run, across 42 monkeypatch/patch call sites.
findings.proposal: create_server(artifacts, *, channels: MarkupChannels), where MarkupChannels bundles the root resolver, channel opener and fact-sink factories with production defaults. Tests pass fakes, and the module-global lambdas and their test-steering docstrings go. Apply the same to verdict_tools.
findings.next_change: Changing how the markup channels resolve the project root or open the escalation queue, for example having the orchestrator pass the main-checkout root explicitly at spawn. The agent must keep the global-name-lookup indirection or the tests silently stop steering the sink and touch the real queue or root. It must read four test files to learn which module globals are load-bearing for them.

findings.statement: cli.py hosts the eval subsystem's drivers rather than just its entry points. 754 of its 2,046 lines are eval code: six click commands plus 15 helpers including the Elo judge loop (_run_judge_cmd), the OFAT/matrix/confirm drivers and _run_plan_only. 34 of cli.py's 47 function-local imports sit in that section. _run_plan_only invokes the architect with hardcoded model='opus', max_turns=50, max_budget_usd=5.0, effort='high', backend='claude' rather than through resolve_route or config. evals/runner.py reaches up with 'from orchestrator.cli import eval_cmd' under __main__, and test_eval_configs.py patches 'orchestrator.cli._run_matrix_cmd'. The load_config/ConfigRequiredError preamble is repeated in 10 commands and the --config option in 11.
findings.proposal: Move the eval commands and drivers into orchestrator/evals/cli.py as a click group that cli.py registers with main.add_command, a downward import. Route _run_plan_only through resolve_route with the eval config. Fold the config preamble into one click callback/decorator.
findings.next_change: Adding an eval stage or changing how eval fixtures are resolved or priced means editing cli.py, the orchestrator's operational entry point, next to run/verify-merge. The agent must know that the plan-only path bypasses model routing, so a routing or allowlist change does not reach it, and that a test pins the private _run_matrix_cmd by dotted path.

findings.statement: The scheduler re-parses the task record's wire shapes inline at every use, although a typed parser exists (shared.task_metadata.parse_metadata, used only by _task_external_deps). Dependency-id normalisation 'str(d.get('id', d) if isinstance(d, dict) else d)' appears 7 times in scheduler.py: _iter_pending_deps_in, _compute_delivered_check_cache, _deps_satisfied ×2, _build_reverse_index, _phase_backfill_dep_status and _phase_backfill_terminal_dep_records. deterministic_runner.py has one more copy and agents/briefing.py a variant. Train-id extraction is hand-written 3 times (tasks_by_train; _deps_satisfied for the task and for the dep). The deterministic-kind test is inlined in _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked and twice in harness.py, despite Scheduler.is_deterministic's docstring calling itself 'the single source of truth'.
findings.proposal: Add shared.task_metadata helpers dependency_ids(task) -> list[str] and train_id(task) -> str | None and use them at every site; call Scheduler.is_deterministic at the inline site.
findings.next_change: A change to the dependency wire shape, such as dict deps gaining a 'project' key or cross-project deps moving into dependencies, must be applied at 9 sites. Missing one makes that gate compute a different dep id than the others. For example, the status backfill could fetch an id the satisfaction check never looks up, so the dependent waits fail-safe indefinitely, and no single test covers all nine readers.

findings.statement: The task-3118 rule that a transport refusal is not a content measurement has one home, metrics.detect_invocation_error, and only 2 of the slice's LLM-scoring call sites use it (runner.run_architect_eval and judge.judge_plan_quality). Three other scoring sites turn any unparseable answer into a scored verdict, and that includes a 429/cap refusal, whose output is not JSON. First, reviewer_trial/scorer.match_issues returns ([], reviewer_issues, cost), so score_panel_run records recall=0, precision=0 and f1=0. The reviewer_trial `campaign` command then caches that record at <results-dir>/trial-N/scores/<variant>__<diff>.json and reuses it on rerun, and campaign.summarize_campaign and report.build_trial_report average it into mean_f1 without any marker. Second, judge.run_judge returns winner='tie', which elo.record_match applies as a 0.5 Elo result and counts toward MAX_PER_PAIR. Third, compare._assess_task returns winner='tie', which is counted in ComparisonReport.ties. All three call invoke_agent directly with no UsageGate, while the panel runner in the same campaign is gated. test_reviewer_trial_scorer.py::test_unparseable_output_still_reports_cost pins the fabricated shape (matches == [], unmatched == reviewer_issues).
findings.proposal: Add one eval-layer call helper built on detect_invocation_error that returns Scored | Refused(cause), and make every scoring site use it. Give ScoringResult, JudgeVerdict and TaskAssessment an explicit unmeasured state. The reducers (campaign.summarize_campaign, reviewer_trial report, elo.record_match, compare_models) then exclude and count those records, as report.py already does for cap_tainted.
findings.next_change: An agent adding the next scorer (a reviewer-trial arm metric, a prompt_opt scorer or a judge variant) copies the dominant local shape: `structured_output or json.loads(output)` with a neutral fallback. Nothing at the invoke boundary says that detect_invocation_error exists or that the fallback fabricates a score. Doing it right means reading runner.run_architect_eval's taint table and metrics.detect_invocation_error, both outside the file being edited. Nothing catches the wrong version: the existing tests feed a non-JSON result and assert the zero/tie shape, and the campaign reducer averages the zero into mean_f1 without a marker.

findings.statement: run_architect_eval is one 870-line async function: 296 code lines and 545 docstring/comment lines. It is the most-changed symbol in the slice. Five policies, each with its own task history, live inline: the per-attempt timeout and cost banking (nested _timed_invoke), the taint table (four except/elif exits deciding tainted vs floored vs judged), plan-judge invocation with invocation/cost stamping, P5 cost resolution with a skip-when-nothing-spent rule, and the terminal-kind/decline read, which must run in the `finally` before cleanup_eval_worktree rmtree's .task-meta. Its collaborators arrive through five function-local imports (invoke_agent, ARCHITECT, TaskArtifacts, the snapshots module, judge.*). The sibling executors run_eval and run_end_to_end use the module-level create_eval_worktree import instead. As a result, orchestrator.evals.runner.create_eval_worktree and orchestrator.evals.snapshots.create_eval_worktree are different patch targets for sibling executors. Tests get in through private names: `_build_eval_usage_gate` appears on 22 lines across test_eval_architect.py, test_eval_driver.py and _campaign_gate_helpers.py, and `_EVAL_CAP_WAIT_SANITY_SECS` is patched to 0.0.
findings.proposal: Split the function into three parts. An invoke step returns a frozen ArchitectAttempt (plan, declines, tokens, cost, error marker, unmeasurable). A pure classify step maps the attempt to tainted, floored or judge and carries the taint table. A pure step assembles the metrics. Inject the worktree, invoke and judge collaborators as parameters so tests stop patching private module names. Move the taint-table and cap-wait rationale to docs/plan-scoring-and-judge.md and leave a pointer.
findings.next_change: Likely next changes are adding a seventh failure cause, scoring with a second plan judge, or changing which exits read declines. The agent has to load 870 lines, 545 of them rationale. It must work out which of four exits reaches which scoring branch and that the decline read has to stay in the `finally` ahead of the worktree cleanup. It must also know the test patch targets differ from the sibling executors'. A wrong edit, such as moving the decline read below the `finally` or changing the tainted predicate in only one branch, is caught only if one of the ~5,500 lines of test_eval_architect.py happens to exercise that exit.

findings.statement: EvalMetrics.role_under_test is a free `str | None`, and its field comment promises "'implementer' for the ordinary path". No producer writes that value. collect_metrics never sets the field, and run_eval stamps only 'judge', by mutating the asdict output, so every implementer cell persists None. There are 3 writers: run_architect_eval sets 'architect' on the dataclass, while run_eval ('judge') and run_end_to_end ('end_to_end') set it by mutating metrics_dict. 8 reader sites compare string literals: report.py ×5, judge_pilot, cli, scripts/run_fable_trial_v2_campaign. The sibling vocabulary EvalConfig.role = {'implementer','architect','judge'} is a different set. report.select_survivors groups rows by role_under_test, and test_eval_driver_report.py builds rows with role_under_test='implementer', a value no real report contains. So select_survivors(roles=['implementer']) on a real OFAT composite report returns []. It has no production caller yet; report.py calls the auto-driver 'NOT yet wired'.
findings.proposal: Define one RoleUnderTest StrEnum shared by EvalConfig.role and EvalMetrics.role_under_test. The executor sets it on the dataclass (collect_metrics takes the role as an argument), never by mutating the dict. Map legacy None at load time.
findings.next_change: The planned OFAT auto-driver is the next change report.py's own comment names. The wiring calls select_survivors(report, top_k, roles=['implementer','architect']) the way the tests do, gets back no implementer survivors, and feeds run_matrix_stage an empty implementer list. Getting it right requires knowing that collect_metrics never stamps a role and that EvalConfig.role and role_under_test are different vocabularies. The tests cannot catch this because they hand-build rows with the unwritten value.

findings.statement: The persisted-cell contract has three parts: the directory evals/results, the filename grammar `{task_id}__{config_name}__{run_id}.json`, and the EvalResult field filter on load. It is defined in runner.save_result and re-derived in 5 other places: runner._result_exists (glob), rereview.py (its own RESULTS_DIR plus _extract_run_id parsing `stem.split('__')`), scripts/run_vllm_eval.py (its own RESULTS_DIR plus the same glob twice), scripts/_eval_results_io.load_results_from_dir, and orchestrator/scripts/backfill_composite_scores.py (its own RESULTS_DIR). scripts/_eval_results_io.load_results_from_dir mirrors load_results over an arbitrary dir because runner.load_results takes no dir argument. Only that copy names a malformed file; runner.load_results raises a bare JSONDecodeError. EvalResult itself, a 9-field dataclass, lives in the 2533-line executor module. So compare.py (module-level import), report.py and judge_pilot.py (TYPE_CHECKING) and the scripts all depend on the module that imports workflow, scheduler and cli.
findings.proposal: Add an evals/results.py store (ResultStore(dir) with save/load/exists/parse_name) that owns EvalResult. runner, rereview, compare, report, judge_pilot and the scripts import it, and the executor module drops out of their dependencies.
findings.next_change: Example: let a campaign write cells to its own results dir, or add the trial to the filename. The agent edits runner.save_result and load_results, but rereview, run_vllm_eval's resume check and backfill_composite_scores keep globbing the packaged dir with their own constants and grammar. Nothing catches the split, because each copy is tested against itself.

findings.statement: run_eval and run_end_to_end share 76 identical code lines out of 110 and 96. The shared run covers worktree creation, task assignment, GitOps/scheduler/stub wiring, gate ownership, build_workflow, the wait_for timeout, outcome mapping, collect_metrics, EvalResult, save_result and gate teardown. The owned-gate `finally` exists in three copies (run_eval, run_architect_eval, run_end_to_end), even though the InjectedGate comment says the contract is stated once because three copies is the shape that drifts. run_eval_matrix re-implements _bounded_fanout's FIRST_COMPLETED monitor and cancellation loop (30 of _bounded_fanout's 36 code lines identical), and _bounded_fanout's docstring says it mirrors that loop 'EXACTLY'. The differences between the two executors are four inputs: initial plan (frozen vs None), briefing class, result label, and post-collect stamps.
findings.proposal: Add one _run_workflow_cell(task, orch_config, *, initial_plan, briefing, label, stamps, usage_gate) and an async context manager for the owned-gate lifecycle that all three executors use. Express run_eval_matrix as thunks over _bounded_fanout, with the skip-existing check inside the thunk.
findings.next_change: Changing timeout semantics, adding a stamp to the frozen-plan path (replay_frame is stamped only by run_end_to_end), or changing sibling-cancellation handling has to be done in two or three places. Tests cover each copy separately (test_runner_matrix.py even reaches _collect_cancel_errors), so a fix applied to one copy passes green while the other keeps the old behaviour.

findings.statement: Upstream, the cause of an unmeasurable cell is a typed value: shared.invocation_outcome's CapHit, AuthFailed, ModelNotFound, ServerError and ZeroOutputWedge. The slice flattens it into free text. metrics.detect_invocation_error writes 'cap_hit: <reason>', 'auth_failed: HTTP n', 'model_not_found: ...', 'api_error: HTTP 429', 'server_error: HTTP n' and 'wedge: ...'. run_architect_eval's except branches add 'timeout: ...', 'cap_exhausted: ...' and 'harness_error: <Type>: ...', and its judge branch adds 'raised: ...'. These are joined as '{stage}:{marker}' with '; ' and persisted. report._taint_cause then parses them back with split(';') and partition(':') to bucket cap_excluded_by_cause, assuming the first marker is the one that drove the exclusion. The cause vocabulary has no single definition. The fixtures in scripts/tests/test_run_fable_trial_v2_campaign.py spell it 'architect: cap_hit' (with a space), which the parser accepts only because it calls strip().
findings.proposal: Persist invocation_error as structured {stage, cause, reason}, with cause drawn from one enum (or from the invocation_outcome variant name), and render the string only at display time.
findings.next_change: Example: add a cause such as budget_exhausted for SessionBudgetExhausted, which campaign_usage_gate's docstring flags as a latent harness_error. The agent must write a producer string that happens to fit the parser's grammar. A misspelled prefix silently becomes its own bucket or 'unknown' in cap_excluded_by_cause, and no type or test ties the producer's prefixes to the consumer's buckets.

findings.statement: Reducing a reviewer artifact to {verdict, issues} means unwrapping the verdict-tool envelope and applying the ERROR-verdict filter, whose canonical home is artifacts.TaskArtifacts.aggregate_reviews. The slice re-implements this five times. scoring._unwrap_verdict_envelope sniffs the shape (schema_version + role + dict verdict), and quality_from_review_artifact zeroes ERROR issues. compare._read_reviewer_verdict_envelopes unwraps envelope['verdict'], and compare.score_result_from_artifacts skips ERROR per reviewer. reviewer_trial/runner._run_single_reviewer unwraps and checks membership in {'PASS','ISSUES_FOUND'}. reviewer_trial/scorer.score_panel_run filters ERROR. rereview checks for ERROR. compare.py and scoring.py carry 4 comment/docstring sentences saying they mirror aggregate_reviews. Verdict states are bare string literals at every site.
findings.proposal: Export one normalizer from artifacts (or verdict_tools) that returns a typed ReviewPayload with a Verdict enum and the ERROR rule applied, and call it from the five eval sites.
findings.next_change: Production adds a verdict state or bumps the envelope schema (a renamed payload key, say) and edits workflow/artifacts. The eval scorers keep the old reading and silently count or drop the new reviews' issues. No test spans the production artifact writer and the eval readers, so the divergence surfaces only as shifted quality numbers.

findings.statement: The panel-result cache is implemented twice: reviewer_trial/runner.run_trial's inner _run_and_save, and __main__._load_or_run_panel, whose docstring says it 'Mirrors the caching logic in runner.py _run_and_save()'. findings.next_change: Adding a field to PanelRunResult (per-reviewer cost, say) requires changing both rehydration sites, and missing one drops the field only on cache hits, which no test exercises across both paths. findings.statement: metrics and judge import each other function-locally. metrics.resolve_terminal_kind imports judge.is_scorable_plan with the comment 'a module-level import here would turn a deliberate one-way function coupling into a real cycle'. judge.judge_plan_quality imports metrics.coerce_cost_usd/detect_invocation_error with the comment 'there is no cycle either way — metrics.py does not import judge', which is false at this tree. metrics.collect_metrics also imports scoring.recovery_score_for_run locally, because scoring imports EvalMetrics/compute_composite from metrics, and scoring imports snapshots locally. That is four deferred intra-slice imports among three peer modules, and two comments disagree about whether a cycle exists.
findings.proposal: Move is_scorable_plan and its produced_a_plan twin to a leaf plan-predicate module that both import. Move collect_metrics, which needs verify, workflow and scoring, out of metrics, so that metrics becomes a leaf of vocabularies and pure functions.
findings.next_change: An agent trusting judge.py's comment hoists `from .metrics import ...` to module level. That works until metrics is imported first on some path, then fails with an ImportError on a partially initialised module, on a path that only some entry points take. Another agent needing a predicate across the pair adds a fifth local import. Only an import-time failure would catch this.

findings.statement: prompt_opt/__init__.py re-exports 34 names from 9 submodules in an `__all__` list maintained by hand. Only 2 test files import through it (6 names in total). Every production importer (engine.py, smoke.py, __main__.py) imports the submodules directly. Because __init__ eagerly imports canary, curator_corpus, smoke and the rest, `python -m orchestrator.evals.prompt_opt` loads every submodule before __main__ runs. __main__'s function-local imports of curator_corpus and smoke therefore defer nothing.
findings.proposal: Drop the re-exports and leave __init__ with only its docstring; point the two tests at the submodules.
findings.next_change: An agent adding a prompt_opt module has to decide whether to extend the 34-entry lockstep list, and a heavy dependency added to any submodule is paid by every import of any prompt_opt submodule. A reader of __main__ is misled into thinking its deferred imports keep the canary command light.

findings.statement:
The recon escalation category vocabulary has three separately maintained homes that must agree:
(a) the string literal at each _escalate call site: 9 distinct categories across 10 calls in harness.py;
(b) _RECON_DEDUP_CONFIG.infra_dedupe_categories (8 entries), which gates both submit_or_dedupe folding and _finding_recently_resolved's 24h suppression;
(c) the 3-entry tuple inside _escalate that picks severity 'info' versus 'blocking'.
Fold identity is a fourth per-call choice: pass a stable finding= dict, or fall back to hashing the summary.

The homes have already drifted. 'recon_resume_failure_storm' (_resume_interrupted_runs) is missing from (b) and passes no finding=, while its summary embeds the count, window and project list. Its three sibling storm alarms each pass a module constant (_DEAD_OWNER_STORM_FINDING, _PLACEHOLDER_DROP_STORM_FINDING, _PHANTOM_CITATION_DROP_STORM_FINDING), documented as existing 'so submit_or_dedupe folds repeated storm alarms into a single pending escalation'. So every resume-failure storm files a fresh pending escalation and is exempt from recently-resolved suppression.

The comment above the config still says it 'covers all four recon escalation categories'. The only test of this alarm (tests/test_harness.py near line 10654) mocks _escalate and counts calls, so it cannot observe folding.

Across reconciliation/, Escalation( is constructed at 11 sites in 8 modules using three dedup mechanisms.
findings.proposal: One typed registry of recon escalation categories mapping each to {severity, folds, identity factory}. _escalate takes the registry key, not a str. _RECON_DEDUP_CONFIG and the severity choice derive from the registry. Add a test that every category literal passed to _escalate is registered.
findings.next_change:
Change: add a recon alarm, for example the consecutive prune-enumeration-failure backstop that TaskKnowledgeSync.run's comment proposes, or a fifth storm counter.

What the agent must know beyond the call site: to register the category in _RECON_DEDUP_CONFIG; to choose severity by editing the tuple inside _escalate's body; to define a stable _*_FINDING constant with variable data kept out of identity fields. The _escalate signature asks for none of these.

What catches a wrong version: nothing before it lands. It passes pyright and the existing tests (which mock _escalate). It surfaces later as unfolded duplicate pending escalations that the port-8103 watcher must close by hand, which is exactly what the resume-failure storm already does.

One policy, 'escalate after N consecutive completed full cycles whose Stage-2 stat confirms a bad value, recomputed from the journal', is implemented twice by copy.

The two copies duplicate line for line, with inverted polarity: the prior-run filter (id != run_id, run_type full, status completed), the defensive re-sort, the stage_reports['task_knowledge_sync'] dict-or-attribute extraction, and the streak+1 >= threshold rule.

The copies file through different policies for the same signal shape. The snapshot streak goes through _escalate (info severity, fingerprint fold, recently-resolved suppression). The growth streak calls escalation_queue.submit directly (level 1, blocking, has_open_l1 on a synthetic task_id).

TaskKnowledgeSync.run's comment already names a third streak, consecutive prune-enumeration failures, 'mirroring the harness's existing consecutive-miss streak', left as 'a possible follow-up'.
findings.proposal: One streak evaluator over journalled runs, parameterised by (stage key, stat key, bad value, threshold, run filter), plus one filing path chosen by policy. Both existing streaks become two declarations.
findings.next_change:

What the agent must do today: write a third extract, compute, evaluate and maybe_escalate quartet. It must pick polarity, the prior-run filter and a filing path, with no rule to choose between the two existing ones.

What catches a wrong version: only unit tests the author writes for the new copy, since nothing shared is exercised. A filter that forgets `id != run_id`, or counts None as a reset instead of a stop, lands silently.

findings.statement:
BaseStage.run calls assemble_payload(events, watermark, prior_reports) -> str. That interface receives no run_id or run window and can return only the payload text. Both concrete stages therefore route per-run data through instance attributes.

TaskKnowledgeSync uses six class-level attributes, each reset at the top of run(), written in assemble_payload, and read back after super().run() returns: _current_run_id, _run_window_start, _stale_missing_run_id_markers, _rescued_in_window_markers, _recon_report_systemic_polled, _stage2_combined_flags. That makes 22 self.* references. Two of the resets carry 'reviewer finding: robustness' comments about a prior run's values leaking. In production that leak cannot occur, because _make_stages builds fresh stages every cycle; only test reuse can trigger it.

MemoryConsolidator does the same with four attributes: _fetch_degraded_sources, _undatable_freshness_records, _entity_summary_snapshot_lines_stripped, _live_workflow_snapshot.

assemble_payload raises a RuntimeError whose message tells tests to assign the private stage._current_run_id. Tests do so at 6 sites in 3 files.

The prior finding on MemoryConsolidator's harness-assigned inputs is the input-side twin. This is the output side of the same interface.
findings.proposal: Pass a frozen per-run context (run_id, run window, model) into assemble_payload, and have it return a small value object (payload text plus side stats). BaseStage.run then merges those stats into the report, removing the instance stashes and the private-attribute test seam.
findings.next_change:
Change: surface one more per-cycle datum from payload assembly into the stage report, for example a count of dropped sections, or let assemble_payload use the run window.

What the agent must do: add a class attribute, a reset in run() before super().run(), a write inside assemble_payload, and a read after super().run(). It must also update every test that calls assemble_payload directly so they poke the new private attribute.

What catches a wrong version: only a test that runs two cycles on one instance. A forgotten reset or a missed read-back is invisible to pyright.

findings.statement:
The LLM-provider axis is a plain-str config field per component (ReconciliationConfig.agent_llm_provider and judge_llm_provider, both defaulting to and configured as 'claude_cli', config.yaml:286/293). Each component routes on it with if/elif string comparisons, and the two handle an unrecognised value differently:
- AgentLoop._call_llm raises ValueError.
- Judge._call_llm's else branch sends any value that is not 'claude_cli' or 'anthropic' (for example a typo 'claude-cli') to the OpenAI SDK. The SDK's errors are not JudgeInfraError, so review_run's broad except returns None with no infra-streak accounting.

The non-CLI branches exist only for the unused providers:
- AgentLoop's anthropic/openai adapters, _OpenAIResponseAdapter, and mutation journaling with CircuitBreakerError. Its sole production caller, verify.py:439, uses claude_cli with six read-only tools, and is_mutation=True appears only in tests/test_agent_loop.py.
- Judge's prose-parsing _parse_verdict path, which its docstring says 'For claude_cli that path is dead'.

Keeping that text path alive keeps the verdict contract in two homes: JUDGE_VERDICT_SCHEMA, and the hand-written '## Output Format' JSON in prompts/judge.py with severities typed as literals.
findings.proposal: Make the provider a Literal or StrEnum validated at the config boundary. Either delete the in-process anthropic/openai paths, with their adapters and the prose output contract, or move provider dispatch behind one shared adapter used by both AgentLoop and Judge.
findings.next_change:
Change: alter the judge verdict contract (add a field, rename a severity) or the CLI invocation.

What the agent must know: that the schema, the prose JSON block, _verdict_from_payload, the text-path _parse_verdict with its fail-closed phantom stamp, and AgentLoop's three adapters all carry the contract. Branches that production never runs still have to be kept consistent.

What catches a wrong version: tests/test_judge.py, which pins the text path (21 provider references), so dead code stays green while the live path's prose and schema can drift apart. A config typo is caught by nothing.

findings.statement: shared/task_statuses.py exists to be the single source of the task-status vocabulary, yet this slice keeps seven hand-written copies of parts of it, and no parity test covers any of them. Status-word regex lexicons: task_filter.COUNT_SNAPSHOT_RE carries two identical alternations, and flag_dedup._COUNT_GROUP_RE carries a third ('done|cancell?ed|pending|in[-_ ]?progress|blocked|deferred|review|total|merge[-_ ]?deferred'). Terminal-status sets {'done','cancelled'}: flag_dedup.TERMINAL_STATUSES, task_filter.INACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES (which gates the stale-status sweep's destructive edge invalidation and the citation-repoint skip) and orphaned_recon_escalation_sweep.TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES. Sort map: task_filter._STATUS_PRIORITY, which lacks infra-hold and cancelled, and which task_knowledge_sync imports as a private name. The infra-hold member (D3) already failed to reach the lexicons: is_count_snapshot('40 pending / 12 infra-hold') returns False, while is_count_snapshot('40 pending / 12 blocked') returns True. The reason the comments give for the copies is false. _COUNT_GROUP_RE says it is a LOCAL copy of task_filter.COUNT_SNAPSHOT_RE 'to honour the no-import-inversion convention (reconciliation must not import from middleware)'. But task_filter is in reconciliation/, has been since its first commit, and flag_dedup already imports it, through a function-local import in _is_task_count_snapshot_finding. _extract_terminal_status cites the same convention, which three reconciliation modules already break.
findings.proposal: Derive the lexicon alternation and the terminal/inactive sets from shared.task_statuses (TaskStatus, TERMINAL), building the regex fragment once in task_filter. Delete flag_dedup._COUNT_GROUP_RE's private lexicon and TERMINAL_STATUSES. Make _STATUS_PRIORITY total over TaskStatus, or derive it from TaskStatus, and extend the parity test to every remaining home.
findings.next_change: Add or rename a TaskStatus member, as infra-hold was added. The agent edits shared/task_statuses.py and its parity test, and both pass. To be correct it must also know about the three regex lexicons, the three terminal sets and _STATUS_PRIORITY, which sit in three recon files that never import the enum. Nothing catches a miss: no test pins these copies, and the failure is silent (a count snapshot not stripped, an edge not retired, a task sorted by fallback).

findings.statement: The two Graphiti edge-retirement sweeps share a copied skeleton rather than one mechanism. That skeleton is: seed a stats dict with the tri-state enumeration_complete and enumeration_incomplete_kind keys; call enumerate_all_valid_edges; record paged.complete BEFORE apply_incompleteness_policy, an order both copies comment as 'load-bearing' because the policy raises on structural incompleteness; flatten_dedup_edges; then loop update_edge(invalid_at=...) with CancelledError/KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit re-raised. The fail-closed rule that an incomplete READ must not become a destructive WRITE is enforced only because each sweep copied the policy call. The second sweep imports the first's private constant (`from ...stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep import _SWEEP_AGENT_ID, flatten_dedup_edges`). The agent-id literal 'recon-stage-memory_consolidator' is hand-written in two slice modules (stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep._SWEEP_AGENT_ID, citation_verifier.REPOINT_AGENT_ID), while stages/base.py and stats_verifier derive it as f'recon-stage-{StageId}'. Each sweep also mints its own parallel stat-key constant pair (STATUS_SNAPSHOT_ENUMERATION_*_STAT_KEY, PRIORITY_OVERRIDE_ENUMERATION_*_STAT_KEY).
findings.proposal: Extract one edge-sweep primitive, for example an async enumerate_complete_edges(memory_service, project_id, log) -> (edges, completeness) that applies the policy and records completeness, plus an invalidate_edges(...) loop. Both sweeps take only their selection rule. The agent id comes from StageId.
findings.next_change: Add a third Graphiti edge sweep. dependency_direction_check already describes dependency-direction assertions that can end in a retired edge, so retiring stale dependency edges is a plausible next sweep. The agent copies one of the two sweeps. It must know four things: the record-before-policy order; that apply_incompleteness_policy must be called because enumerate_* never raises; the private _SWEEP_AGENT_ID; and the consolidator projection of a new stat-key pair. If the policy call is dropped, a page-capped read retires live edges. That is caught only if the author also writes an incomplete-enumeration test.

findings.statement: A finding's task_id is an LLM-authored string that is routinely comma-composite (e.g. '3105,4223'). Each consumer parses it with its own rules, and the meanings differ. In this slice: _decompose_suppression_task_id splits suppression rows; _canonicalize_suppression_task_id requires int or isdigit components; compute_flag_signature folds cited_tasks in and sorts lexicographically; _is_valid_marker_task_id splits and isdigit-checks; flag_task_ids.task_id_components is the shared flag-side splitter. server/recon_report.py has two more, with a numeric sort. filter_suppressed decomposes only the ROW side and compares the flag's task_id verbatim (`tid_str = str(flag_tid)`). So an operator's blanket suppression for 3105 does not reach a flag carrying '3105,4223' or '3105, 4223'. preservation_specimen_guard's docstring names this gap as a reason it had to decompose ids itself ('Inheriting that gap would make this guard zero-recall'). The commit that introduced the shared splitter (d03334582d, 'one flag task-id splitter for both flag-side consumers') left filter_suppressed outside it.
findings.proposal: Parse the flag's subject once at the dedup boundary into a typed value (components tuple plus optional fp key) built on flag_task_ids. Suppression matching, marker-key validation, signature building and suppression canonicalization then all read that value instead of re-splitting strings.
findings.next_change: An operator or agent silences a recurring finding with write_suppression_record(task_id=3105), as was done for task 3105, and the finding keeps returning because Stage 1 emits a composite id. An agent fixing this must reconcile five parsers with different validity rules. It must also see that the signature folds cited_tasks while suppression does not, and that fp: keys share the column. No test states which composite semantics suppression should have.

findings.statement: task_filter.py's name and module docstring ('filtering and formatting the Taskmaster task tree') describe only its second half. Its first half is an unrelated unit: the recon-prose grammar library. That covers COUNT_SNAPSHOT_RE, the temporal-framing, batch-plan, conflicting-status, live-status, present-tense-completion and proposed-resolution detectors, TASK_REF_RE, and the WIDE/STRICT clause boundaries, whose blast-radius rationale runs about 120 comment lines. Their consumers are write gates in server/tools.py, middleware/dependency_direction_check (an edge-retiring path), services/completion_claim_gate, both Graphiti sweeps and four scripts. The two halves share no state. Importers split cleanly by half, and the module also carries a private alias (_CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE) kept alive for one script. The grammar is also why middleware imports reconciliation, the reverse of the layering flag_dedup's comments assert.
findings.proposal: Move the grammar half into its own module (e.g. reconciliation/recon_prose_grammar.py) that imports nothing from task_filter. task_filter keeps FilteredTaskTree and the render functions. Neither half imports the other, so heuristic 13 holds for both files.
findings.next_change: Change the task-reference grammar (TASK_REF_RE, e.g. admit a new 'T-94' spelling) or a clause boundary. The agent must find a grammar that drives a destructive edge sweep and soft-block write gates inside a module named for task-tree filtering, and must read the allowlist argument to know which boundary each consumer may take. Only the out-of-module WIDE_CLAUSE_BOUNDARY_RE allowlist test guards a wrong choice. The reverse also costs: an agent changing task-tree rendering loads 775 lines of grammar it does not need.

findings.statement: The prior finding does not record that the uniform mechanism already exists. FlagTypeFamily (added by 12bf41ab0f, 2026-09-28, task 5271) carries the measured spellings, family-tolerant matches() and a drift log (log_drift). It is used by 3 vocabularies: CLUSTER_GROWTH_FAMILY, PREMATURE_WIDENING_CAVEAT_FAMILY, and sweep_deletion_guard's EVIDENTIARY_ANCHOR_DELETION_FAMILY. The other flag_type-keyed gates in the slice use four other mechanisms: exact frozenset membership (STALE_METADATA_, ABSENCE_, PHANTOM_TASK_CREATION_, AUTHORSHIP_SUSPICION_FLAG_TYPES), a precomputed canonical-family set (STALE_BULK_GET_STATUSES), an exact literal (_is_systemic_pattern_candidate, 'systemic_pattern') and substring stems (_flag_type_in_grounds_family, preservation STRANDED_FLAG_TOKEN_FAMILY). findings.statement: ReconReportState keeps one fact in several mutable maps and holds them consistent by hand in every mutator: which findings exist in a run and under which dedup key. The run-level maps are _state, _active, _run_sig_index, _run_finding_index, _run_desc_index and _run_cited_task_index. Each _ReportEntry adds two mirrors (_signature_to_finding, _deschash_to_finding), and _persist_run/_serialize_entry add two persisted 'slices' of the run indices. Keys are computed at registration in add_finding and cite_task, then recomputed from the finding's fields in _purge_finding to undo them. tick releases them wholesale, hydrate_from_store rebuilds them by union, and _persist_run re-derives the slices. No single register/unregister operation owns the invariant 'every index entry names a live finding owned by exactly one reachable entry'. Instead it is narrated in docstrings that cite prior breaches. _reachable_run_entries documents that before task 4653 mutations of evicted-but-indexed entries were 'silently dropped on the way to the store', and that identity-deduping let a 'stale twin' overwrite the live row. add_finding's docstring proposes a fourth index to be 'maintained alongside _run_sig_index'.
findings.proposal: Extract a RunFindingIndex value that owns the key derivation and the maps. It would expose register(finding, entry), unregister(finding), release(run_id), owned_slice(entry) and from_rows(rows). ReconReportState would call only those methods, and the per-entry mirrors and persisted slices would be derived from it, not maintained alongside it.
findings.next_change: The plausible next change is a new dedup key (the per-run {task_id: flag_types} index add_finding's docstring already proposes), or a new mutator such as re-targeting a finding. To get it right the agent must know all six run maps, both per-entry mirrors and both persisted slices, plus five places to update: register in add_finding or cite_task, unregister in _purge_finding by recomputing the same key from the stored finding, release in tick, rebuild in hydrate_from_store, and slice in _persist_run. It must also respect the _reachable_run_entries reach rule. A miss surfaces only when a scenario test happens to cover an evict-then-mutate or restart-then-refile path. The three task-4653 fix commits are that pattern.

findings.statement: Project scope has no single parse step at the MCP boundary. Each tool body opens with its own subset of _resolve_identity, _canonicalize_project_id_arg, validate_project_id, _known_project_gate and _backlog_gate for project_id tools, or _normalize_project_root (which returns str | dict) for project_root tools. Seven of the 35 tools that take project_id never canonicalize it. Four of them carry a copied docstring note telling the agent to 'Pass the canonical (underscore) spelling', and trigger_reconciliation forwards the raw spelling to task_interceptor.buffer.request_trigger. _halt_payload re-canonicalizes internally to compensate. Its comment says get_status and trigger_reconciliation 'do not' canonicalize, so a hyphen id would answer halted: False beside halted_projects: ['know_live']. trigger_reconciliation names the canonical id in its remedy because 'unhalt_reconciliation does not canonicalize'. The registry gate is equally per-tool. Five of the eleven graph-mutating tools apply _known_project_gate (delete_episode, redact_episode_content, update_edge, reassign_edge, ensure_entity_node). Six do not (delete_entity, merge_entities, rename_entity, set_entity_summary, refresh_entity_summary, rebuild_entity_summaries).
findings.proposal: Declare scope per tool, for example @scoped('project_id', write=True) or a registry consulted by the dispatch wrapper that already sits at ToolManager.call_tool (markup_guard). findings.statement: The shutdown budget invariant is false at this tree, and the test that claims to guard it hand-counts a step list that has grown. _FORCE_EXIT_BUDGET's comment states the worst case as drain(5)+close(5)+sqlite_watchdog(5)+event_queue(5)+harness_cancel(25)+memory_close(20)+journal_close(5) = 70s, under 75s. _graceful_shutdown actually runs 11 _run_shielded steps. Nine of them use the default _CLEANUP_STEP_TIMEOUT: task_interceptor.drain, task_interceptor.close, curator_usage_gate.shutdown, curator_cost_store.close, sqlite_watchdog.close, event_queue.close, taskmaster.close, recon_journal.close and recon_ledger.close. That gives a worst case of 9x5 + 25 + 20 = 90s, past the 75s force-exit budget. tests/test_server_shutdown.py::TestShutdownBudgetArithmetic computes '5 * _CLEANUP_STEP_TIMEOUT + harness + memory_close' from a literal 5 and passes. config/schema.py carries _MIRROR_FORCE_EXIT_BUDGET as a third copy of the same arithmetic's inputs.
findings.proposal: Make the shutdown sequence a declared tuple of (name, closer, timeout). _graceful_shutdown iterates it, and the budget assertion (test and schema validator) sums the same tuple, so the invariant is computed rather than restated.
findings.next_change: The plausible next change is another shutdown step. topic_cluster_store, for example, is closed ad hoc in run_server's finally block. The agent has to update the comment sum, the literal 5 in the test and possibly _FORCE_EXIT_BUDGET and schema.py's mirror, and must notice that the force-exit plus systemd invariant depends on it. Today nothing fails: the test multiplies a constant it does not derive, and four earlier step additions went through unnoticed.

findings.statement: run_server (826 lines) wires MemoryService, TaskInterceptor, TargetedReconciler and the journal through post-construction setters and attribute assignment, so features are armed by the order of calls in one function, not by construction. Its comments name four features that stay 'DORMANT until wired' or that degrade 'with no test failure' when a line is deleted or reordered: the closure gate via _wire_closure_collaborators, the audit-trail archive, the known_projects storm alarm via set_known_projects, and the lifecycle-reset filer. TaskInterceptor is constructed in two arms, reconciliation enabled (11 kwargs) and disabled (7 kwargs), and three wirings are repeated in both. Later code tests variable existence with "'event_buffer' in locals()" and "'ticket_store' in locals()" because the arms bind different names.
findings.proposal: Build the collaborators first and pass them through constructors, using a frozen assembly record if the list is long. Fold the two TaskInterceptor arms into one builder that takes optional reconciliation components, so 'both arms wire X' holds by construction and the locals() probes disappear.
findings.next_change: The plausible next change is a collaborator that MemoryService or TaskInterceptor needs, such as another escalator that needs known_projects, which is how set_known_projects arrived (task 3088). The agent must find the right arm or arms and the right position relative to initialize() and start(). It must also know that omitting the call leaves the feature inert, not broken. Only some wirings have a capture test (TestClosureCollaboratorWiring). The comment says the known_projects wiring is 'KNOWINGLY UNCOVERED'.

findings.statement: Escalation filing does blocking filesystem I/O: EscalationQueue construction, a get_by_task directory scan and an fsync-flushed submit. The rule that a write path must call it off the event loop lives only in call-site docstrings, and the slice applies it inconsistently. tools.py::create_mcp_server's _file_triage_fail_open_storm wraps emit_triage_fail_open_storm_escalation in asyncio.to_thread under 'ASYNC ON PURPOSE — do not re-inline'. Its sibling _report_unverified_claims calls emit_unverified_claim_escalation directly on the loop from add_memory and add_episode, and that emitter also ends in file_folded_escalation. markup_guard's sinks (emit_markup_residue_escalation, emit_markup_storm_escalation) are likewise synchronous and invoked from the async dispatch wrapper. memory_service offloads its four equivalent emitters, each with its own 'LOAD-BEARING' comment.
findings.proposal: Give the filer one async entry point, an afile_folded_escalation that does the to_thread hop itself, and make the emitters async. Async callers then cannot reach the blocking body, and the call-site comments go away.
findings.next_change: The plausible next change is another storm or claim alarm filed from a write path, a pattern that already recurs eight times. The agent must learn from a neighbouring call site, not from the emitter it calls, that the emitter blocks. Only the production loop-lag monitor (task 3778) catches a wrong version, after it ships.

findings.statement: Whether Taskmaster is configured is encoded twice inside create_mcp_server. One encoding is a boolean (_taskmaster_configured = task_interceptor is not None). The other is a null object: around line 8118 the captured name task_interceptor is rebound to TaskInterceptor(None, None, _fallback_buffer). Closures read captured variables at call time, so every helper defined above the rebinding sees the null object at runtime, and a natural 'task_interceptor is None' guard there is always False. _batched_task_statuses' docstring exists to warn about exactly that. The two encodings also produce three error_type spellings for 'not configured': ConfigurationError for the tool-body literals, RuntimeError from TaskInterceptor._ensure_taskmaster via mcp_tool_errors, and ConfigError for the ticket store in task_interceptor.
findings.proposal: Bind the interceptor once at the top of create_mcp_server, as either the real one or the null object, and derive configured from it. Emit one 'not configured' error_type for every unconfigured backend.
findings.next_change: The plausible next change is a new gate or helper above the task-tool section that reads task state. The prior candidates were the premature-completion, completion-claim and citation gates, all written this way. The agent must know to guard on _taskmaster_configured and not on the name pyright types as Optional. A deployment without Taskmaster then raises RuntimeError instead of failing open. findings.statement: Write-time control flags travel inside the persisted metadata payload, and each forwarding tool strips its own subset. The flags are allow_mcp_markup, allow_near_duplicate, allow_dangling_citations and _causation_id. add_memory strips allow_mcp_markup (strip_markup_override) and pops allow_near_duplicate. add_system_record and consolidate_memories strip only allow_mcp_markup before cleaned_meta becomes stored metadata, or the base of the canonical's metadata. allow_near_duplicate or allow_dangling_citations passed to either is therefore persisted onto the record. _extract_causation, the 'single point where the caller's metadata becomes persisted state', strips only _causation_id.
findings.proposal: Define one WRITE_TIME_CONTROL_KEYS set and have _extract_causation return the typed flags alongside a payload stripped of all of them. Tools then read flags from the parsed value, not from metadata.get(...) is True.
findings.next_change: The plausible next change is a fifth override flag (literal-True semantics), the pattern that already produced three. The agent must add a strip in every metadata-forwarding tool. Nothing catches a miss before the key lands in Qdrant; memory_metadata's census warns about an unknown key only after persistence.

Into metadata it merges only three curator_* keys (curator_action, curator_justification, combined_at). metadata.files is the typed field: shared/task_metadata.py declares files: list[str], and candidate_key, the phantom-done gate, lock_charter_guard.extract_files and orchestrator lock derivation all read it. It keeps the target's pre-combine value. The comment at the write says 'readers parse it back from the FILES_TO_MODIFY marker — kept for compatibility with existing parsers', but no .py file anywhere parses that marker, so the comment states something false (heuristic 1). The same combine re-embeds the target into the curator corpus with rt.files_to_modify (CandidateTask.from_rewritten_task in _dispatch_ticket_decision). The vector store and the task store therefore disagree about the target's files. The marker also leaks verbatim into memory summaries: fused-memory/tests/fixtures/e2_distractor_slab.jsonl holds real 'Details: FILES_TO_MODIFY:' completions. Repeated combines nest the marker.
findings.proposal: Write the union into metadata.files through the sanctioned files sanitizer in the same update_task, stop prefixing details, handle DuplicateCandidateKeyError explicitly (combine-into-survivor or audited refusal), and delete the false comment.
findings.next_change: An agent fixing 'combined task under-declares its files' would add files=rt.files_to_modify to combine_metadata. It must know four things beyond this method. Under metadata_mode='merge' that key overwrites wholesale, which is the right union semantics. SqliteTaskBackend.update_task recomputes candidate_key from files via _files_for_key, so a combine can now raise DuplicateCandidateKeyError, and _execute_combine's bare 'except Exception' turns that into None, a silent degrade to create. module_charter.sanitize_files_for_persist is the sanctioned writer of metadata.files (commit 9535b253b8). The pool renderer feeds the old marker back to the LLM inside details. Nothing catches a wrong version: no test asserts metadata.files after a combine, and git grep finds the marker only in a memory fixture.

findings.statement: Seven readers decide which metadata key carries a task's declared files, under at least four different rules. (1) backends/sqlite_task_backend.py::_files_for_key takes files if not None, else files_to_modify, list-only; it feeds candidate_key and the UNIQUE index. (2) TaskInterceptor._extract_meta_files_from_meta takes files, else files_to_modify on a falsy value, coerces a str to [str], type-guarded; it feeds CandidateTask and therefore the curator's in-memory dedup key TaskCurator._normalize_key. (3) task_curator.py::_task_files reads top-level files_to_modify, then metadata.files or files_to_modify, with no type guard; it feeds the corpus pool and backfill. (4) task_interceptor.py::_extract_metadata_files reads files only, list-only, dict metadata only; it feeds the phantom-done gate and reconciliation/targeted.py. (5) lock_charter_guard.extract_files reads files only. (6) TaskInterceptor._extract_deliverable_signals_from_meta takes the union, deliberately. (7) shared/briefing_queries.py reads files only. _normalize_key's docstring says it delegates to compute_candidate_key, 'the single owner of this key definition'. Its input is not single-owned. A schema-valid blob {files: [], files_to_modify: ['a.py']} gives a store key over [] while the curator keys over ['a.py']. A str-valued files gives ['a.py'] to the curator and [] to the store and the done gate. Even inside task_interceptor.py the key list exists twice: the _DELIVERABLE_SIGNAL_KEYS constant and the literal ('files', 'files_to_modify') in _extract_meta_files_from_meta.
findings.proposal: One declared_files(metadata) -> tuple[str, ...] (and a named declared_files_union for attribution) homed below both packages' callers, e.g. beside shared.task_metadata or middleware/candidate_key.py. Every reader above calls it, and candidate_key and _normalize_key take its output.
findings.next_change: Plausible next changes are retiring the files_to_modify alias, accepting a scalar files string, or adding module_charter sanitisation at read time. Any of them means finding all seven readers across four modules and two packages, and nothing points from one to the others. The store/curator divergence is invisible to tests. No test computes SqliteTaskBackend's candidate_key and TaskCurator._normalize_key for the same metadata and compares them. The pre-LLM exact-match cache and the UNIQUE index would silently disagree about task identity.

findings.statement: When the wait expires, resolve_ticket returns {'status': 'failed', 'reason': 'timeout'}, even though the ticket row is still 'pending' and the worker may still create the task. A post-wake read of a still-pending row returns 'failed'/'server_closed' the same way. The public status vocabulary (created, combined, failed, refused) has no 'undecided' value. One token 'failed' therefore covers terminal failures (curator_failed, bad_candidate_json, worker_dead) and outcomes that are not yet decided. The MCP docstring (server/tools.py resolve_ticket) lists timeout among 'failed' reasons and advises 'retry or report an error'. orchestrator/agents/roles.py::submit_resolve_instructions tells agents to pass timeout_seconds=60 and to report 'failed', while a single curation may take CuratorConfig.timeout_seconds=180 and a batch up to batch_timeout_cap_seconds=360.
findings.proposal: Return a distinct non-terminal status (e.g. 'pending' with the ticket id) for timeouts and post-wake pending rows, and reserve 'failed' for terminal ticket rows. Update the MCP docstring and roles.py instructions in the same change.
findings.next_change: An agent adding retry-on-failure to a filer, or making Stage-2 count outcomes, branches on status=='failed'. To do it correctly it must know that reason in {timeout, server_closed} means 'maybe still coming' and the other reasons mean terminal. That fact lives only in this method's body. Resubmitting on a timeout duplicates the task unless the caller supplies escalation_id+suggestion_hash for the R4 check, and nothing catches the duplicate: the curator may see the first task only after it lands.

findings.statement: TaskInterceptor._process_add_ticket (209 lines) is a complete second single-ticket worker pipeline with no production caller. Commit 48f658ea5e (2026-04-23) removed the worker's 'await self._process_add_ticket' and the worker now calls only _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared. Tests keep it alive, and four live docstrings and comments still describe it as a production path. Its own docstring says 'The worker calls this'. _dispatch_ticket_decision says it is 'shared by both worker paths (_process_add_ticket and _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared)'. _curator_lock lists it under 'Taken by', and the route_deterministic comment names it. The same pattern covers _process_add_tickets_batch (20 lines, 'historical entry point used by tests'), _merged_audit_metadata (26 lines, whose docstring describes a 'separate tm.update_task(metadata=…)' audit write that task 2649's set_status_and_stamp_audit replaced) and TaskCurator._intra_batch_key (whose docstring says it is 'Used by the planning_mode / curator batch pipeline'). The paths have already diverged. On CancelledError, the dead path persists the terminal row through _persist_worker_terminal under asyncio.shield. The live batch path re-raises and leaves the ticket pending.
findings.proposal: Delete _process_add_ticket, _process_add_tickets_batch, _merged_audit_metadata and _intra_batch_key. Retarget their behavioural tests to submit_task/resolve_ticket over a real TicketStore. Port the cancellation-persistence hardening to the batch dispatcher if it is still wanted.
findings.next_change: An agent changing R4 idempotency, degrade-reason propagation or cancellation persistence reads _process_add_ticket because its docstring says the worker calls it, and edits there. The 14 tests that drive it go green and production behaviour does not change. Task 1316 already did exactly this. To avoid it, the agent must know from git history that the batch-prepared method is the only live path.

findings.statement: Batch size is a dimension of variability implemented as parallel copies at every curator layer, not as one mechanism. At the pipeline layer the prior finding already shows curate() and curate_batch_prepared() encode the guard order twice. At the prompt layer, _build_user_prompt and _build_batch_section render the identical candidate block and pool. At the invocation layer, _call_llm and _call_llm_batch each build the same invoke_with_cap_retry call: model, disallowed_tools=['*'], no_mcp_servers_config, strict_mcp_config, permission_mode, cap_wait_sanity_secs, transcript scope. They also each build the same 11-keyword CuratorFailureError with a near-identical message. The decision parser is the one layer already shared (_parse_decision_dict).
findings.proposal: Make single curation a batch of one at the prompt and invocation layers: one candidate-section renderer (header parameterised), one _invoke_curator(prompt, schema, timeout, turns, budget, label), and one failure-to-CuratorFailureError mapper. This collapses the two pipelines after that.
findings.next_change: Plausible changes: adding a field the LLM should see (execution_class is hashed into payload_hash but rendered by neither builder), adding an invoke kwarg (routing/effort), or adding a CuratorFailureError attribute that CuratorEscalator reports. Each needs two edits, and the agent must know the batch twin exists. Size-1 worker batches go to curate() -> _call_llm while larger ones go to _call_llm_batch, so a change made to one twin is exercised only for some traffic. Tests built around one entry point do not cover the other.

findings.statement: After any update_task carrying prompt/title/description/details, the interceptor re-embeds the task from an inline CandidateTask(..., files_to_modify=[]) built from the refreshed row. The task's Qdrant point is therefore re-upserted with embedding_text(title, description, []) and payload files_to_modify=[], which erases the file contribution that record_task and backfill_corpus put into both the vector and the payload. Downstream, TaskCurator._fetch_entry_for_neighbor's thin fallback derives module_keys=[] from that payload, search_corpus reports files_to_modify [] for the hit, and ZOT duplicate sweeps compare against a vector composed differently from their query. The class already has the right constructor, TaskInterceptor._build_candidate(task), which index_committed_tasks uses for exactly this get_task-shaped dict and which reads metadata.files.
findings.proposal: Use _build_candidate(refreshed) for the update-path re-embed and assert files_to_modify in the re-embed test.
findings.next_change: Replace the inline construction with TaskInterceptor._build_candidate(refreshed). The agent must know that get_task returns metadata already decoded to a dict (_row_to_task) and that _build_candidate reads kwargs['metadata']. The existing test passes either way, so a regression test must assert the files reaching reembed_task.

findings.statement: The candidate_key uniqueness scope, 'non-cancelled rows of the same tag', is defined in _migrate_v3_to_v4's CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE candidate_key IS NOT NULL AND status != 'cancelled'. It is re-spelled as a SQL literal in the migration audit queries and in every live write path. Each write path also re-implements 'collision -> survivor lookup -> DuplicateCandidateKeyError': add_task's pre-INSERT guard and IntegrityError arm, update_task's pre-UPDATE guard and IntegrityError arm, and _write_status_and_verify. The IntegrityError arms classify the exception by substring ('candidate_key' not in str(exc)). The pre-write guards run only while the index is absent (the degraded window), so a predicate drift between them and the index shows up only in that window.
findings.proposal: One module constant for the predicate SQL plus one async _raise_candidate_key_collision(conn, tag, key, exclude_id=None). Classify IntegrityError by index name (sqlite reports it), not by substring.
findings.next_change: Plausible changes: narrowing uniqueness (e.g. letting a done task's key be re-filed) or adding a second partial index. The index DDL, four audit queries and five write-path SELECTs must change together, or the str(exc) sniff misattributes the new index. A missed guard copy disagrees with the index only while the index is absent, which tests rarely set up.

findings.statement: TaskInterceptor holds its backend as TaskBackendProtocol, but the status and audit writes it depends on most go to three methods the protocol does not declare: set_status_and_stamp_audit (every reopen and every done with provenance), stamp_audit_metadata (the done-provenance repair) and rewrite_audit_trail (recon audit rotation). All three are called through '# type: ignore[attr-defined]', so pyright cannot check their signatures at the call sites. The interceptor's test fixture stubs set_status_and_stamp_audit with AsyncMock, which accepts any arguments. The protocol docstring calls itself 'The 12-method + lifecycle surface'. It declares 21 members. The backend docstrings justify keeping the privileged writers 'off the 12-method contract'.
findings.proposal: Declare a second narrow protocol (PrivilegedAuditWriter) for the three writers. Type the interceptor's dependency as both protocols and drop the ignores. Use create_autospec-style doubles in the fixture.
findings.next_change: Adding a parameter to set_status_and_stamp_audit (e.g. a provenance writer identity) or renaming audit_fields breaks the interceptor at runtime, with pyright silent and the AsyncMock-based suite green. Only end-to-end tests over a real SqliteTaskBackend (e.g. orchestrator/tests/test_reopen_sticks_e2e.py) would notice.

findings.statement: The durable-queue payload is an untyped dict. Its field set is an implicit wire contract that 4 producers write and 7 consumers read and mutate. There are 4 producers: add_episode (15 keys), add_memory's Graphiti leg (9), replay_from_store (6) and _dual_write_callback (7). The 7 consumers are _execute_graphiti_write, _execute_mem0_write, _execute_mem0_classify_and_add, _dual_write_callback, _refresh_summaries_callback, _report_queue_dead_letter and _decode_referents, plus durable_queue.py, which itself reads '_write_op_id' and the 'add_episode'→'uuid' identity key. The contract rests on three unstated conventions. First, executors POP 8 keys (_causation_id, _write_op_id, temporal_context, unverified_claim, uuid, referents, reference_time, plus the queue's own key reads). Callbacks then read 3 of those popped keys back (_causation_id, temporal_context, unverified_claim). That only works because DurableWriteQueue._process_item deliberately parses the JSON a SECOND time for the callback ('A FRESH parse, deliberately not `payload`: _execute_write pops journal metadata that the callbacks read back out'). Second, producers disagree on which keys exist: add_memory's Graphiti payload carries no project_id, so _refresh_summaries_callback falls back group_id→project_id→'main'. Third, the 'uuid' key is load-bearing negative space, and three docstrings plus a pop-and-warn defend its absence. No type names the 18 keys, and pyright cannot see a misspelled key.
findings.proposal: Define one frozen QueuedGraphitiWrite / QueuedMem0Fact dataclass, or TypedDict with total=True, per operation in a leaf module next to durable_queue. Each needs to_json/from_json with explicit back-compat defaults for legacy rows. Producers construct it, executors receive the typed value rather than popping, and the callback gets the same immutable value. That removes the double-parse convention.
findings.next_change: Likely change: thread one more per-write fact through the queue, the way temporal_context, unverified_claim and referents were each added. The agent has to edit every producer dict literal (add_episode, add_memory, replay_from_store and possibly _dual_write_callback's derived payload). It then has to decide pop versus get in the executor, and know that pop is safe only because durable_queue re-parses for the callback. It also has to know which producers omit project_id and that 'uuid' must never appear. Nothing catches a missed producer: the key is silently absent and reads as default on the old rows. A misspelled key is caught only if a test happens to cover that producer.

findings.statement: MemoryService is built in two phases, and its durable queue goes live before its collaborators exist. initialize() calls DurableWriteQueue.initialize(), which runs _recover_in_flight and _start_workers_for_pending_groups (durable_queue.py L370-372), so queued backlog rows start executing immediately. Seven collaborators are wired only afterwards, by server/main.py. Write journal: set_write_journal, about 8 lines later. taskmaster: assigned as a public attribute at L630. Known-project registry: set_known_projects at L698. Then set_recon_journal and set_recon_ledger (L797/801) and set_event_buffer (L882). Rows drained in that window run with partial state. _record_queue_terminal_outcome returns early with no journal, so the terminal write-back is lost. _check_dependency_direction returns [] silently when self.taskmaster is None; there is no log, unlike its sibling _known_projects miss, which WARNs. Dead-letter and repair-storm escalations are refused with a WARNING because _known_projects is empty. The class compensates piecemeal. Two queue hooks are bound methods 'for call-time resolution' because of this ordering, as their docstrings state. self._write_journal is None-guarded 24 times, and set_known_projects logs a 'permissive' INFO line because 'an empty registry is a real window'.
findings.proposal: Pass the always-present collaborators (journal, known-projects snapshot, taskmaster handle) to the constructor, or to initialize(). Start queue workers in an explicit start() that main.py calls after wiring is complete. The remaining genuinely optional collaborators (recon ledger, event buffer) can then keep None semantics deliberately rather than by accident of ordering.
findings.next_change: Likely change: add another collaborator that a queue executor or post-write pass needs, for example a ticket store or a second registry. By precedent the agent adds a None attribute, a set_x() and a call in main.py. It then has to discover on its own that queued rows can run before the setter fires, and decide per call site whether None means skip, warn or fail. Nothing catches the window: tests construct the service and wire it synchronously before enqueueing, so the startup-drain interleaving is never exercised.
